The words

O that the Lord would guide my ways
To keep His statutes still!
O that my God would grant me grace
To know and do His will!

O send Thy Spirit down to write
Thy law upon my heart!
Nor let my tongue indulge deceit,
Nor act the liar's part.

From vanity turn off mine eyes;
Let no corrupt design,
Nor covetous desires arise
Within this soul of mine.

Order my footsteps by Thy Word,
And make my heart sincere;
Let sin have no dominion, Lord,
But keep my conscience clear.

Assist my soul, too apt to stray,
A stricter watch to keep;
And should I e'er forget Thy way,
Restore Thy wand'ring sheep.

Make me to walk in Thy commands, 'Tis a delightful road;
Nor let my head, or heart, or hands, Offend against my God.

How to sing it from the solfa

  • Find doh first. Play or hum Ab and sing d r m f s up from it, so the whole choir has the key in their ears before you start.
  • Pitch the first note. The tune starts on s, (E♭), on the word “O”, as a pickup before the first full bar.
  • Count the time. 3/2 means three minim beats in each bar. In the grid every cell is half a crotchet: a dash (–) holds the note before it, and _ is a rest.
  • Know the notes. The tune uses d r m f s l. A comma after a note (s,) is the octave below; an apostrophe (d') is the octave above.

About the hymn

The words are by Isaac Watts, first published in 1719. The tune, EVAN, is by William Henry Havergal (1847). This version of the melody and the words comes from the Open Hymnal Project.

  • Words (1719): Isaac Watts (1674–1748)
  • Music (1847): William Henry Havergal (1793–1870)

Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune EVAN by William Henry Havergal (1793–1870); words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748). The Open Hymnal Project publishes this hymn as public domain; NoteFusion's engine wrote the solfa from its notes. The melody has not yet been checked against a printed hymn book.

Questions about O That the Lord Would Guide My Ways

What is the doh of O That the Lord Would Guide My Ways?

In this version, in Ab major, doh is Ab. If your choir sings it in another key, doh moves to the new key note and every solfa syllable stays the same — that is what movable doh means.

What note does O That the Lord Would Guide My Ways start on?

It starts on s, (E♭ in Ab major), a pickup on the word “O” before the first full bar. Find doh first, then sing up or down to s,.

Is O That the Lord Would Guide My Ways in the public domain?

Yes. Isaac Watts died in 1748, William Henry Havergal died in 1870; the words were first published in 1719 and the music in 1847. Everyone named died before 1955 and both were published before 1929, so the hymn is out of copyright in Nigeria, the UK, the EU and the United States. Modern arrangements and translations can still be under copyright.
